questions.explanation_english: Bose- Einstein Condensation –: Bose- Einstein condensation is a phenomenon that occurs when a dilute gas of bosons is cooled to a temperature very close to absolute zero. At this temperature, the individual particles lose their distinct identities and merge into a single quantum state, forming a coherent matter wave. Hydrogen is composed of two particles, a proton and an electron. Both protons and electrons are fermions not bosons. Fermions follow the Pauli Exclusion Principle, which states that no two identical fermions can occupy the same quantum state simultaneously. Therefore, hydrogen cannot exhibit Bose-Einstein condensation.

questions.question_english: Which of the following atoms cannot exhibit Bose- Einstein condensation, even in principle?
questions.question_hindi: इनमें से कौन सा परमाणु बोस-आइनस्टीन संघनन हो या सिद्धान्त में भी प्रदर्शित नहीं हुआ है?
questions.explanation_english: Bose- Einstein Condensation –: Bose- Einstein condensation is a phenomenon that occurs when a dilute gas of bosons is cooled to a temperature very close to absolute zero. At this temperature, the individual particles lose their distinct identities and merge into a single quantum state, forming a coherent matter wave. Hydrogen is composed of two particles, a proton and an electron. Both protons and electrons are fermions not bosons. Fermions follow the Pauli Exclusion Principle, which states that no two identical fermions can occupy the same quantum state simultaneously. Therefore, hydrogen cannot exhibit Bose-Einstein condensation.
